"""A tiny notes service: GET /notes lists the notes, GET /health answers once the database does."""

import json
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

import psycopg

DATABASE = "host=127.0.0.1 user=postgres dbname=postgres"


class Notes(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        with psycopg.connect(DATABASE) as connection:
            if self.path == "/health":
                connection.execute("select 1")
                self.reply({"ok": True})
            elif self.path == "/notes":
                rows = connection.execute("select id, body from notes order by id").fetchall()
                self.reply([{"id": note_id, "body": body} for note_id, body in rows])
            else:
                self.send_error(404)

    def reply(self, payload: object) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(payload).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 8000), Notes).serve_forever()

"""Users of the notes service, for chronobox's hand-off replays (``[handoff]`` in chronobox.toml).

    python3 traffic.py            # write a note every 0.1 s and read the list, until stopped
    python3 traffic.py --report   # after: fail if a note the users were told was saved is missing

A write counts as saved once its insert committed; failed writes and reads are only counted
(a restart may fail a few), but a saved note that is gone is lost data.
"""

import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

import psycopg

DATABASE = "host=127.0.0.1 user=postgres dbname=postgres"
SAVED = Path("/tmp/traffic-saved")
FAILED = Path("/tmp/traffic-failed")
PAUSE_S = 0.1
READ_EVERY = 5


def write(number: int) -> None:
    """Save one note, and record it as saved only once the insert committed."""
    try:
        with psycopg.connect(DATABASE, connect_timeout=2) as connection:
            connection.execute("insert into notes (body) values (%s)", (f"traffic {number}",))
    except psycopg.Error:
        with FAILED.open("a") as failed:
            failed.write(f"write {number}\n")
        return
    with SAVED.open("a") as saved:
        saved.write(f"traffic {number}\n")


def read() -> None:
    """List the notes through the service, as a user's page would."""
    try:
        urllib.request.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:8000/notes", timeout=5).read()
    except OSError:
        with FAILED.open("a") as failed:
            failed.write("read\n")


def report() -> int:
    """Exit status: 1 if a saved note is missing from the table."""
    saved = set(SAVED.read_text().splitlines()) if SAVED.exists() else set()
    with psycopg.connect(DATABASE) as connection:
        rows = connection.execute("select body from notes where body like 'traffic %'").fetchall()
    missing = saved - {body for (body,) in rows}
    failed = FAILED.read_text().splitlines() if FAILED.exists() else []
    print(f"{len(saved)} notes saved, {len(missing)} of them missing; {len(failed)} failed requests")
    return 1 if missing else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if sys.argv[1:] == ["--report"]:
        sys.exit(report())
    for number in range(1, sys.maxsize):
        write(number)
        if number % READ_EVERY == 0:
            read()
        time.sleep(PAUSE_S)

# A small notes web app and its PostgreSQL database, on chronobox's default image.
#   uv run chronobox-mcp --project examples/notes
image = "default"
prepare = [
  "install -d -o postgres -m 700 /var/lib/postgresql/data",
  "su postgres -c '/usr/lib/postgresql/15/bin/initdb --no-instructions -A trust -D /var/lib/postgresql/data'",
]
setup = ["python3 migrate.py"]

[machine]
mem_mib = 1024
disk_mib = 2048

[project]
exclude = ["__pycache__"]

[[service]]
name = "db"
start = "su postgres -c '/usr/lib/postgresql/15/bin/postgres -D /var/lib/postgresql/data -c listen_addresses=127.0.0.1'"
ready = "pg_isready -q -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres"
workdir = "/"

[[service]]
name = "app"
start = "python3 app.py"
ready = "curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8000/health"

# What `verify_script` adds to every replay of a hand-off.
[handoff]
load = "python3 traffic.py"                 # users keep writing and reading during the replay
load_check = "python3 traffic.py --report"  # no note they were told was saved may be lost
compare = [                                 # what the agent tested must be what the script makes
  # (each dump has its own random \restrict key)
  "pg_dump --schema-only -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres postgres | grep -vE '^.(un)?restrict '",
  "curl -s 127.0.0.1:8000/notes | python3 -c 'import json, sys; print(sorted(json.load(sys.stdin)[0]))'",
]

# For the demo: users writing a note every 0.1 s, the whole session long.
[[service]]
name = "users"
start = "python3 traffic.py"
ready = "test -s /tmp/traffic-saved"
after_setup = true

content.text:
`notes` now has a required `title` column on the running server, and `GET /notes` returns it. After the migration, the 272 notes users had saved were all still there.

- **Existing notes:** all of them now have a title taken from the first three words of their body, and none are null. For example, "buy milk" gives the title "buy milk" and "traffic 1" gives "traffic 1".
- **Users writing meanwhile:** the clients that insert notes don't send a title, so a plain `NOT NULL` column would have made every one of their writes fail. I added the column as nullable, plus a trigger that fills the title from the body on insert when none is given. I then backfilled the old rows and set `NOT NULL`. I rehearsed this first on a fork of the live machine with writers running, and nothing failed.
- **App:** `app.py` now returns `id`, `title` and `body`. I restarted the app after the migration.
- **Failed requests:** 2 requests failed, probably during the app restart. I didn't check the logs to confirm.
- **`migrate.py`:** I updated it to include the same column, trigger and backfill, and it's safe to re-run.

An insert that supplies its own title keeps it, because the trigger only fills in a missing one.
